purpose: Hero concepts for the Key project blog article.

concepts.title: Approve once, keep working
concepts.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: finished landscape hero concept for a developer's technical blog post about Key, an open-source macOS CLI secret manager inspired by Unix pass. Generate a single wide landscape image approximately 16:9. Core story: keep working in the terminal and coding-agent workflow while approving protected secret access with the native Apple ecosystem. Scene: a quiet real developer workspace with a contemporary silver MacBook and the user's left wrist wearing an Apple Watch in the near foreground; one natural, anatomically correct relaxed hand resting beside the trackpad, no additional hands. The Watch shows a tiny restrained native-looking system approval notification represented mainly by a simple confirmation glyph, not an invented elaborate app. The laptop screen contains a tasteful dark terminal workspace, with the single clearly legible command '$ key get services/api' and a small row of masked bullets below it; a second understated pane suggests a coding conversation with abstract muted lines, not legible prose or a robot. A subtle fingerprint glyph may appear in a small native-style approval sheet on the screen, but do not crowd the scene with authentication widgets. Key has no separate watch app in this concept; the watch approval is an OS interaction. Premium editorial photography, three-quarter close view, gentle afternoon light, brushed aluminum, slate screen, warm neutral desk, believable imperfect tactile details, amber reflection on glass, quiet confidence. Hardware, wrist and terminal form one cohesive subject, with breathing room for a responsive article crop. Avoid hacker aesthetics, green matrix text, hooded figures, server racks, giant locks, floating shields, security badges, holograms, logos on the desk, promotional headlines, subtitles, watermarks, real credentials, or extravagant neon. The intended feeling is secure and native yet low-friction, not a dramatic cybersecurity advertisement.

concepts.title: Secrets with an address
concepts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: wide landscape editorial hero concept for Key, a macOS terminal-first secret manager inspired by pass. Produce a single finished 16:9-style image. Core idea: passwords, TOTP seeds and API credentials deserve a small well-ordered home with convenient path names, instead of being scattered through .env files. Scene: a beautifully crafted compact brushed-aluminum file organizer on a warm ivory desk, like a modern Mac accessory interpreted as an editorial sculpture. Three individually separated dark slate file cards sit neatly within it, each with one precise small monospace path label: 'services/api', 'accounts/personal', 'github/totp'. Do not print secret values. The cards have subtle sealed edges or discreet patterned surfaces to suggest individual encryption. Integrated into the organizer's front edge is one small dark glass fingerprint approval surface with a delicate warm illuminated rim, representing Mac-native user-presence protection. A single fine graphite path line leads from the organizer toward an understated small terminal pane in the background, whose only text is '$ key get services/api', with masked dots below; keep the physical object dominant and the terminal secondary. Elegant product still life blended with conceptual editorial illustration, tangible material grain, precise construction, soft contact shadows, restrained cream, aluminum, graphite and pale blue palette. Calm, spare and clear at thumbnail size. The illustration is a metaphor, not a hardware product or a UI screenshot. No literal app icons, giant keys or padlocks, cloud logos, robot mascots, cyberpunk effects, noisy circuit boards, marketing copy, title typography, watermark, identifiable real secrets, or many tiny unreadable elements. Preserve generous margins for responsive cropping.

concepts.title: One source, many worktrees
concepts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: wide landscape editorial hero illustration for Key, an open-source macOS CLI secret manager designed for people working in coding agents, terminals, branches and worktrees. Generate a single finished landscape image approximately 16:9. Visual metaphor: one trustworthy protected source underneath several independent coding workspaces. Build an elegant minimal isometric physical composition on a matte dark graphite ground. Near the lower center, a compact solid brushed-aluminum vault-folder form contains a few stacked sealed document slips, with a small fingerprint approval medallion integrated into its front, warm subtle human-presence light. From that single source, three tidy thin branching channels, resembling the topology of a Git working tree, lead toward three slim floating terminal-window objects across the upper half. Their small window labels read exactly 'main', 'feature/api', and 'fix/auth'. Each window contains just a few restrained monospace code strokes and masked bullets, not readable secrets or fake dense code. On the central source, a tiny engraved command reads 'key'. One node is a visibly human-controlled approval boundary at the vault; the branches do not claim separate per-agent authorization or isolation. The image should convey that path-addressed secrets stay organized in one protected home and remain convenient to use across development contexts. Premium architectural model and editorial still-life aesthetics, delicate realistic shadows, machined aluminum, subtle pale blue channels, a restrained amber approval accent, no glowing sci-fi. Balanced geometry and strong hierarchy, enough negative space to breathe, readable from thumbnail size. No people or faces, no robot icons, no Apple/Codex/Claude logos, no giant padlocks, no shield badges, no matrix text, no server farms, no marketing headline or watermark. This is an evocative workflow metaphor rather than a literal security architecture diagram. Keep all primary objects comfortably within the frame for responsive cropping.
